scope: Independent apparent geocentric solar-longitude to crossing-instant fixtures, not independent natal-birth to next-year Solar Return reports.
expectationPolicy: Target longitudes and expected UTC instants are transcribed from external sources. Never regenerate them with the application engine or widen tolerances to match its output.

usno-seasons-2022.provider: U.S. Naval Observatory, Astronomical Applications Department
usno-seasons-2022.longitudeConvention: Apparent geocentric solar ecliptic longitude of date: March equinox 0 degrees, June solstice 90 degrees, September equinox 180 degrees, December solstice 270 degrees.
usno-seasons-2022.timeScale: UTC; the retrieved output displays UTC+02:00 with daylight saving disabled.
usno-seasons-2022.utcConversion: Subtract exactly two hours from each published local timestamp; publishedLocal below includes that fixed +02:00 offset.
usno-seasons-2022.versionNote: The retrieved source does not state an ephemeris or model version.
usno-seasons-2022.sourcePrecision: Event times are published to the minute; each target longitude is the exact seasonal-event definition.
usno-seasons-2022.toleranceRationale: The predeclared 120-second bound allows minute-resolution publication and differences between the independent ephemeris models. It is not a claim of 120-second uncertainty in the provider's calculation.

jpl-horizons-2020.retrievalDateBasis: Recorded in the existing src/lib/engine/engine.test.ts provenance header; no fresh ephemeris query was used to create this fixture.
jpl-horizons-2020.queryNote: The repository retains the value, epoch, quantity and centre, but not the original full query URL or response headers.
jpl-horizons-2020.longitudeConvention: Quantity 31: apparent geocentric observer ecliptic longitude of date, IAU76/80, including light-time and aberration.
jpl-horizons-2020.timeScale: UTC at this 2020 epoch. Horizons UT before 1962 is UT1; historic repository vectors are deliberately excluded here.
jpl-horizons-2020.versionNote: The original Horizons ephemeris and EOP version headers are not retained in the repository.
jpl-horizons-2020.sourcePrecision: The solar longitude is retained to seven decimal places in degrees at the specified exact UTC epoch; this is inversion of a positional datum, not a rounded published event time.
jpl-horizons-2020.toleranceRationale: The predeclared 60-second bound allows differences between the independent apparent-longitude models; the printed longitude precision alone is much finer. Expected time remains the literal external epoch.
